Sordina uses accessibility for three things only: stopping a braked app the moment it comes to the front (and its website in the browser too), locking the screen with a double tap, and typing a phrase for you where apps don\'t accept it from outside (Home Assistant Assist, Signal). It only listens to the apps you braked and, if they have a website, to browsers: of those it reads only the address bar, while they\'re in front. It looks at the screen only for a few seconds, only in that app. Nothing leaves the phone.

Every day Sordina prepares a copy of your settings, stickers, brake history and what it has learned. Your phone\'s Google backup takes it to your account, when the phone is charging and on Wi-Fi. Held notifications and the Home Assistant token stay on the phone.\n\nFor this to work, Google backup must be on: Settings › Google › Backup › “Backup by Google One”. Your phone keeps playing. Just softer.

In music, the sordina is the mute: a small piece resting on a violin’s bridge or slipped into a trumpet’s bell. The instrument doesn’t stop playing. It plays softer, warmer, closer. Italians say “in sordina” for doing something quietly, without fuss.

A phone is a wonderful instrument, but it always plays at full volume. Sordina doesn’t switch it off or take it away: it rests a mute on it. What matters gets through, the rest waits for its moment. Nothing is lost, it’s just quieter.
